evals.prompt: sapiens mode. I have to review PR #142 tomorrow morning and I haven't followed it at all. what's it about? the branch is feat/retry-queue
evals.expected_output: A 3 to 5 sentence orientation in full-grammar plain English. No walkthrough of every change. Any extra depth (review status, open questions) is offered in one line instead of delivered.

evals.prompt: sapiens mode. test_checkout_flow.py keeps failing on CI but passes fine on my machine. been stuck since standup, can you figure out why?
evals.expected_output: The cause and the fix stated in the first sentence, in the present state. No narration of the investigation steps and no restating of the symptom the user already described.

evals.prompt: sapiens mode. clean up the scripts/ folder — delete the old migration helpers we don't use anymore and tidy whatever's left. ping me when done
evals.expected_output: At most one message before the final report. But the file deletions get full plain detail before they happen, naming exactly what will be removed, because core rule 7 overrides the speaking budget.

prompt: sapiens lead. the image upload bug from yesterday — what happened with it?
sapiens dev. the image upload bug from yesterday — what happened with it?
sapiens geek. the image upload bug from yesterday — what happened with it?
evals.expected_output: Three answers to the same question, all in full sentences. Lead: outcome and direction only, no file or function names. Dev: plain explanation, a technical term or name only where the reader needs it to act. Geek: real function and file names, precise cause and effect, denser but still one idea per sentence. Length and interruption frequency do not change between levels; only technical detail does.

evals.prompt: sapiens mode. quick look at auth/session_refresh.py before I merge — anything wrong?
evals.expected_output: A short review that still reports BOTH findings: the swallowed save exception (a session can be rotated and then silently lost), and the weaker one — rotate_id runs before save, so a failed save leaves the old id already invalid, which may or may not be safe depending on store semantics. The weak finding is stated with its uncertainty, not dropped to keep the reply short. Dropping it fails check 7.
